display.title: Tanya Shiur 50: Chapter 33, The Joyful Chapter
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 33: serving Hashem with joy, the difference between bitterness and sadness, and the true unity of Hashem as the key to simcha.
display.summary_long: Shiur 50 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, on Tanya chapter 33, 'the joyful chapter'. It asks how the Torah can command 'serve Hashem with joy', and answers that true joy comes only from something true and lasting: Torah and mitzvos. Tanya chapter 1 shows that sadness is the most dangerous state, and the class reviews the difference between healthy bitterness, which leads to action, and sadness, which must be driven away. The Rebbe once chose lines from this chapter for children to recite at the Lag BaOmer parade. The class then studies the chapter's meditation on Hashem's true unity: the 'lower' and 'higher' ways of seeing the world, illustrated by the vastness of the heavens measured in light-years, and by a story of the Mitteler Rebbe, who refused to admit a mysterious visitor. The world before and after Creation is the same before Hashem, and dwelling on this brings deep joy. After a sign-off, the next session recaps, contrasts plain unity with true unity, and explains through the mashal of speech, thought and the heart's desire how the world, created by Hashem's word, is completely nullified to Him, with a story of the Arizal's hour-long vision.
display.lesson: Real, lasting joy comes from contemplating that nothing exists apart from Hashem; such joy drives away sadness and fills one's service of Hashem.

segments.title: The joyful chapter: how can joy be commanded?
segments.summary: Serving Hashem with joy is a command because Torah and mitzvos are a true reason for joy.

segments.title: Sadness versus bitterness
segments.summary: Tanya chapters 1 and 31: sadness is the root of failure, while bitterness that leads to action is welcome.

segments.title: Chapter 33 at the Lag BaOmer parade
segments.summary: The Rebbe chose lines from this chapter for children to recite at the parade.

segments.title: Joy through contemplation
segments.summary: A person's power to picture ideas deeply in the mind brings feelings into the heart.

segments.title: Hashem's true unity and the size of the heavens
segments.summary: The lower and higher views of unity, and the vastness of the universe measured in light-years.

segments.title: The Mitteler Rebbe and the mysterious visitor
segments.summary: Every blade of grass has a mazal above; the Mitteler Rebbe refused to admit a stranger, for reasons revealed later.

segments.title: Before and after Creation, and the recipe for joy
segments.summary: Before Hashem the world is as nothing, as before Creation, and contemplating this brings joy.

segments.title: Plain unity and true unity
segments.summary: The next session recaps, then contrasts setting aside one's will before the Creator with seeing that nothing exists apart from Him.

segments.title: The mashal of speech, thought and the heart
segments.summary: Letters of speech are nullified to letters of thought, and those to the heart's desire.

segments.title: The Arizal's hour-long vision
segments.summary: What the Arizal saw in an hour would take eighty or ninety years to tell.

segments.title: Creation by Hashem's word is nullified to Him
segments.summary: The world, made with Hashem's letters, has no existence apart from Him.
